item.title: Concordia to extend contract with food provider with ties to ICE | News
item.description: Concordia University will be renewing its contract with U.S.-based food provider Aramark for another year, despite student voting to abolish exclusive contracts with the company in 2024. Student advocates today say they are concerned with Aramark’s ties to ICE and use of prison labour in the U.S.

item.title: Montreal’s $40 million investment in police cameras raises privacy concerns | News
item.description: Policing researchers and community advocates oppose Montreal’s planned police body and security camera implementation, pointing to the technology’s ineffectiveness, high costs and potential privacy concerns.

item.title: Hundreds rally in Longueuil against police brutality | News
item.description: Around 300 demonstrators gathered in Longueuil to protest police brutality, call for abolition and denounce the killing of 15-year-old Nooran Rezayi by Longueuil police in September 2025.

item.title: Stingers 3, Bison 1: Concordia kicks off the national championship | Sports
item.description: The Concordia University women’s hockey team opened the U Sports women’s hockey national championship with a win over the University of Manitoba.

item.title: Carabins 5, Stingers 2: Concordia’s magical season ends in heartbreak | Sports
item.description: The Concordia University women’s hockey team competed in their fourth national championship game in five years, but lost a crushing final to its conference rivals.

item.title: Hands that carry Eid | Fringe Arts
item.description: As Eid al-Fitr ends, henna artists reflect on the work, connection and magical experience behind every design.

item.title: Jeux Urbains takes over the Eaton Centre | Sports
item.description: For five days, the 2026 edition of the Jeux Urbains turned the heart of downtown Montreal into a showcase of athletic prowess.

item.title: AI destroys critical thinking in university and beyond | Opinions
item.description: The overall decline in critical thinking at post-secondary institutions due to the rise of generative artificial intelligence is absolutely outrageous.

item.title: Concordia to increase compulsory fees for Fall 2026 | News
item.description: The Concordia Board of Governors approved two per-credit fee increases for students in another attempt to reduce the university’s stark deficit.

item.title: ‘Drop the charges now’: Sit-in at McGill University in support of student protestors | News
item.description: Over 50 protesters performed a sit-in in front of the James Administration Building at McGill University on March 25. The sit-in was organized in response to criminal charges being placed on a group of 13 activists for Palestine who were arrested for occupying the same building in 2024.

item.title: Smart city or watched city? | Opinions
item.description: Surveillance tools are everywhere around us, collecting our personal information and enabling the mass analysis of our data. This leads us to question where our privacy stands and what implications these technologies will have on society.

item.title: A look inside CFBA’s fashion show | Fringe Arts
item.description: CFBA’s fashion show is built on many months of design, experimentation and personal storytelling, reflecting each designer’s vision beyond their fabric.

item.title: Speculative Futurisms takes shape at CUJAH annual conference | Fringe Arts
item.description: From perfume-making to Indigenous futurisms, CUJAH’s annual conference highlights how art can challenge dominant narratives and reimagine the future through collective practice.

item.title: Tatreez workshops rewrite narratives around connection and belonging | Fringe Arts
item.description: Every spring, McGill University’s Quebec Public Interest Research Group invites its community to become involved in fostering social change with a series of events blending creativity with activism.

item.title: Hundreds of Montreal students participate in march against austerity | News
item.description: Hundreds of students from across Montreal marched against austerity and education cuts as part of a week of action that saw 65,000 Quebec students go on strike.
